So I have had this problem in my head for the last week and I havn't found a satisfying anwser yet.

Two partners are in a relationship. (lets call them John and Joan). On a scale both have an attractivness rating of 7 out of 10 points. This rating includes all traites that make you more attractive to the other sex (or the same sex in a gay relationship) . The rating thus includes intelligence, social stance, fame, looks, money etc.

Now the interesting part. Over night one John goes up on the scale to a 9, the other one stays at 7.

A. Would it be immoral for John who is now more attractive to find a new partner with a corresponding attractivness rating of 9?

Alternative scenario: Both Partners are a 7 on said scale. Overnight John drops in attractiveness to a 5.

B.Is Joan now obliged to stay with him?

What does VOAT think?

On question A I thought that it wouldn't be immoral because he would just take the best thing he could get.

i'm not really sure though
The question to begin with has no real and final answer because morality is relative to the individual.
I don't know how to answer this with such an arbitrary scale. It would be easier to discuss with logical transition in question.
Attractiveness? Intelligence? Cleanliness? Because I would have a different answer for different qualities that fluctuate.
It was under the premise, that all factors are accumulated in one rating.

I'd say yes it's immoral for A and no, she doesn't have to stay with him for B. Because I think it is understandable to leave someone if they become uglier, you chose to be with somebody who looked like a 7/10 and he/she became someone who looked like a 5/10, that's not what you signed up for. For A nobody becomes uglier, you still have what you initially liked.
So your anwser to A is that it's immoral for him to ditch the partner for a better fitting partner?
Yes, because I think you shouldn't ditch someone just because you can get better.

I think this question is hard to answer, because it is ignoring the fact that John and Joan are both people with feelings. Sure, John might be more attractive than Joan, but he also might love Joan. I know plenty of people that are in a relationship with someone who is far more attractive/unattractive than they are. This is also ignoring the fact that attraction isn't a consistent 1-10 scale. Different people are attracted to different things, and so what is a 9 for someone might only be a 6 for someone else.

So I'm response to your question, A. I think it would be immoral for John to find someone more attractive, and B. Joan never has a obligation to stay but if she still loved John then she would.
It sounds easy until when it's numbers but there is so much involved when you transition into the real world

I think that if your relationship has anything at all to do with physical appearance, it's in some serious trouble. So I don't think the more attractive person in either case morally may leave the other. The way I work is that I will always find the people I love beautiful, and I will always find the people I strongly dislike a little ugly. If someone doesn't operate like that, I don't want to date them in the first place. Honestly, it seems non-ideal for appearance, intelligence, whatever to matter in a mate. Love isn't about getting the best you can get, it's about picking one imperfect human and deciding, through thick or thin, that this is your human, and you can trust each other no matter what hardships you go through. To do otherwise is really dickish imho.
I don't think anyone is ever obligated to stay with someone. If you don't want to be with them than you are wasting both of your time. Same goes the other way.
